title: Arima 3C with PacBio HiFi Sequencing Library Preparation Protocol
author: Gulhan Kaya
materials: Quantify using Qubit dsDNA HS assay .
Carefully discard supernatant without disturbing pellet.
Quantify DNA using Qubit DNA HS assay.

1. Repair and A-Tailing of digested 3C DNA This step repairs DNA damage and adds A-tails in a single reaction to prepare for adapter ligation. Repair Master Mix: 4 μL Repair Buffer 1 μL End Repair Mix 0.5 μL DNA Repair Mix 24.5 μL Digested 3C DNA Sample Total Volume: 30.0 μL Instructions: Mix the Repair Master Mix gently. Briefly spin down the mix to collect liquid. Add 5.5 µL Repair Master Mix to 24.5 µL DNA (final 30 µL). Gently mix the samples and spin briefly to collect contents. Set up the thermocycler with the following program: 30 minutes at 37°C 5 minutes at 65°C Hold at 4°C 6. Move to the next step of the protocol.

Use the thermocycler with the following program: 30 minutes at 20°C Hold at 4°C Cleanup with 1X SMRTbell Cleanup Beads Add 42.5 μL of room-temperature beads to the samples. Mix beads with the samples thoroughly. Spin briefly to collect liquid. Let the samples sit at room temperature for 10 minutes to bind DNA. Place samples on a magnetic rack until beads separate. Remove the supernatant carefully without disturbing the beads. Add 200 μL of 80% ethanol to the beads, wait 30 seconds, and remove ethanol. Repeat the ethanol wash step. Dry the beads by: Removing residual ethanol while on the magnet. Briefly spinning and placing back on the magnet.

3. Amplification and Cleanup Amplify DNA fragments with adapters on both ends and clean them using 1X SMRTbell Cleanup Beads. PCR Master Mix : 50 μL 2x Xtreme Buffer 20 μL dNTPs (2 mM each) 4 μL Twist UDI primers (plate) 2 μL KOD Xtreme Hot Start DNA Polymerase 24 μL Adapter-Ligated Sample Total Volume: 100 μL Instructions: Mix the PCR reagents thoroughly. Spin briefly to collect the liquid. Add 76 μL of PCR mix to each sample, ensuring a final volume of 100 μL. Mix samples and spin briefly. 5. Use the thermocycler with this program: 94 °C — 2 min (1 cycle) 98 °C — 10 sec (10-12 cycles) 58.8 °C — 30 sec (10-12 cycles) 68 °C — 10 min (10-12 cycles) 68 °C — 7 min (1 cycle) Hold at 4°C DNA Input and PCR Cycles: - 1 ng: 14 cycles - 5 ng: 12 cycles- 10 ng: 11 cycles- 20 ng: 10 cycles - 50 ng: 8 cycles Cleanup with 1X SMRTbell Cleanup Beads Add 100 μL of beads to the samples. Mix thoroughly and spin briefly. Let the samples sit for 10 minutes at room temperature to bind DNA. Place on a magnetic rack and remove supernatant. Wash beads twice with 200 μL of 80% ethanol, waiting 30 seconds each time before removing ethanol. Dry beads as before and resuspend in 50 μL of elution buffer. Incubate for 5 minutes, then separate beads on the magnet. Transfer the supernatant to a new tube for the next step.

4. Repair and A-Tailing of Amplified DNA This step prepares amplified DNA by repairing damage and adding A-tails for SMRTbell adapter ligation. 500-600 ng input or more for Revio or Vega sequencing 250 ng input or more for Sequel II/IIe sequencing Repair Master Mix: 8 μL Repair Buffer 2 μL End Repair Mix 1 μL DNA Repair Mix 49 μL Amplified DNA Total Volume: 60.0 μL Instructions: Mix the Repair Master Mix gently to combine. Spin briefly to ensure all liquid is collected at the bottom. Add 11 μL of the mix to each sample for a final volume of 60 μL . Mix gently and spin briefly to collect liquid. Use the thermocycler with the following program: 30 minutes at 37°C 5 minutes at 65°C Hold at 4°C 6. Proceed to the next step in the workflow.

5. SMRTbell Adapter Ligation and Cleanup This step ligates the SMRTbell adapter to the ends of the amplified DNA fragments. Ligation Master Mix: 4 μL SMRTbell Adapter* 15 μL Ligation Mix 1 μL Ligation Enhancer 60 μL Repaired Amplified DNA Total Volume: 80.0 μL * Exclude the SMRTbell adapter if using the SMRTbell adapter index plate 96A Instructions: Mix the ligation components thoroughly. Spin briefly to collect liquid. Add the prepared mix to the repaired DNA sample. Mix gently and spin briefly. Use the thermocycler with this program: 30 minutes at 20°C Hold at 4°C Cleanup with 1X SMRTbell Cleanup Beads Add 80 μL of cleanup beads to the sample. Mix thoroughly and spin briefly. Let the sample sit for 10 minutes at room temperature to bind DNA. Place on a magnetic rack and remove the supernatant. Wash beads twice with 200 μL of 80% ethanol, waiting 30 seconds each time before removing ethanol. Dry beads as before and resuspend in 50 μL of elution buffer. Incubate for 5 minutes, then separate beads on the magnet. Transfer the supernatant to a new tube for the next step.

6. Nuclease Treatment This step removes un-ligated, semi-ligated, or damaged DNA fragments from the sample. Nuclease Master Mix: 5 μL Nuclease Buffer 5 μL Nuclease Mix 40 μL SMRTbell Ligated DNA Total Volume: 50.0 μL Instructions: Mix the nuclease components thoroughly. Spin briefly to collect liquid. Add the nuclease mix to the ligated DNA sample. Mix gently and spin briefly. Use the thermocycler with this program: 15 minutes at 37°C Hold at 4°C Cleanup with SMRTbell Cleanup Beads (1X) Add 50 μL of cleanup beads to the sample. Mix thoroughly and spin briefly. Let the sample sit for 10 minutes at room temperature to bind DNA. Place on a magnetic rack and remove the supernatant. Wash beads twice with 200 μL of 80% ethanol, waiting 30 seconds each time before removing ethanol. Dry beads as before and resuspend in 50 μL of elution buffer. Incubate for 5 minutes, then separate beads on the magnet. Transfer the supernatant to a new tube for the next step.

2. Ligation of Linear Amplification Adapter and Cleanup This step adds the amplification adapter to DNA fragments. Ensure cleanup beads are at room temperature before starting. Ligation Master Mix: 2 μL Twist universal adapter 10 μL Ligation Mix 0.5 μL Ligation Enhancer 30 μL End-Repaired Sample Total Volume: 42.5 μL Instructions: Gently mix the Ligation Master Mix. Spin briefly to collect the liquid. Add 12.5 µL ligation master mix (Twist universal adapter + ligation reagents) to the 30 µL end-repaired sample (final 42.5 µL). Mix samples gently and spin briefly. 5. Use the thermocycler with the following program: 30 minutes at 20°C Hold at 4°C Cleanup with 1X SMRTbell Cleanup Beads Add 42.5 μL of room-temperature beads to the samples. Mix beads with the samples thoroughly. Spin briefly to collect liquid. Let the samples sit at room temperature for 10 minutes to bind DNA. Place samples on a magnetic rack until beads separate. Remove the supernatant carefully without disturbing the beads. Add 200 μL of 80% ethanol to the beads, wait 30 seconds, and remove ethanol. Repeat the ethanol wash step. Dry the beads by: Removing residual ethanol while on the magnet. Briefly spinning and placing back on the magnet. 10. Resuspend the beads in 24 μL of elution buffer. 11. Spin briefly, then incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature. 12. Place samples back on the magnet and transfer the supernatant to a new tube.

steps.title: Crosslink cells (standard input)
steps.instruction: Harvest 5–10 × 10⁶ cultured mammalian cells, pellet, and remove supernatant. Resuspend in 5 mL RT 1× PBS, add 286 µL 37 % formaldehyde (or 714 µL if using 16 % formaldehyde) to obtain 2 % final formaldehyde, invert gently 10× and incubate 10 min at RT. Add 460 µL Stop Solution 1 (or 497 µL for 16 % formaldehyde), invert 10×, incubate 5 min at RT, then place on ice 15 min. Pellet cells, discard supernatant, wash with 5 mL 1× PBS, aliquot 1 × 10⁶ cells per tube, pellet, remove all residual liquid, snap‑freeze on dry ice or liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Crosslink cells (low input)
steps.instruction: Collect ≤1 × 10⁶ cells in a 1.7 mL microfuge tube, pellet (500 g, 5 min, RT) and discard supernatant. Resuspend in 1 mL RT 1× PBS containing 3 % BSA, invert 5×. Add 57 µL 37 % formaldehyde (≈2 % final), invert 10×, incubate 10 min at RT with occasional inversion. Add 91.9 µL Stop Solution 1, invert 10×, incubate 5 min at RT, place on ice 15 min. Pellet (500 g, 5 min, 4 °C or RT), discard supernatant, wash once with 1 mL 1× PBS + 3 % BSA, invert 5×, pellet again, discard supernatant, remove all residual liquid, snap‑freeze on dry ice or liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Determine DNA yield per million cells
steps.instruction: Thaw one 1 × 10⁶‑cell aliquot. Add 209.5 µL master mix consisting of 174 µL Elution Buffer, 10.5 µL Buffer D, 25 µL Enzyme D and 3 µL (unspecified component). Add 20 µL Buffer E and incubate 55 °C 30 min → 68 °C 90 min → 4 °C hold. Purify with 150 µL AMPure XP beads, elute in 20 µL Elution Buffer, quantify DNA with Qubit dsDNA HS assay, and calculate the number of cells required to obtain ~3–4 µg DNA for the Arima reaction.

steps.title: Cell lysis
steps.instruction: Resuspend one reaction of crosslinked cells in 20 µL Lysis Buffer (tube or PCR plate well) and incubate 15 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Chromatin conditioning
steps.instruction: Add 24 µL Conditioning Solution, mix gently by pipetting, and incubate 10 min at 62 °C (set thermal‑cycler lid to 85 °C if used).

steps.title: Stop reaction
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL Stop Solution 2, mix gently by pipetting, and incubate 15 min at 37 °C (lid 85 °C if using a thermal cycler).

steps.title: Restriction enzyme digestion
steps.instruction: Prepare a master mix per reaction: 11 µL Water, 9 µL Buffer H, 8 µL Enzyme H (total 28 µL). Add 28 µL master mix to each reaction.

steps.title: Sequential incubations
steps.instruction: Mix gently by pipetting and incubate sequentially: 37 °C 60 min → 65 °C 20 min → 25 °C 10 min (lid 85 °C). Optional: extend the 37 °C step or hold overnight if needed.

steps.title: Add Enzyme D master mix
steps.instruction: Add 10.5 µL Buffer D and 25 µL Enzyme D (total 35.5 µL) to each reaction, mix gently. (Equilibrate Enzyme D to RT before use.)

steps.title: Add Buffer E and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL Buffer E, mix gently, then incubate 55 °C 30 min → 68 °C 90 min → 25 °C 10 min (lid 85 °C). Do not exceed 90 min at 68 °C unless a heated lid is used; the 25 °C step may be replaced by an overnight hold at 4 °C.

steps.title: Choose DNA purification method
steps.instruction: Select either Phenol–Chloroform Extraction (more labor‑intensive, higher purity) or SPRI Bead Purification (simpler, comparable yield). Proceed with the chosen method for downstream cleanup.

steps.title: Post‑digestion mix and QC
steps.instruction: Mix the post‑digestion sample gently by inversion (white particles are normal). Transfer 10 µL to a new tube labeled “Digestion QC”, store at –20 °C for later QC analysis, and continue with the remaining sample.

steps.title: Add Enzyme C master mix
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL Water, 70 µL Buffer C, and 12 µL Enzyme C (total 92 µL) to each reaction, mix gently, and incubate 15 min at RT.

steps.title: Phenol‑chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Cool the sample on ice after reverse cross‑linking, transfer to a DNA LoBind tube, add an equal volume of chilled phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (25:24:1) in a fume hood, mix on a vertical rotator (~20 rpm) for 10 min (or invert 20–30 times). Transfer to Phase‑Lock Gel tubes (recommended) and centrifuge 16,000 × g, 15 °C for 15 min. If not using Phase‑Lock tubes, ice the tube 2 min until the organic layer becomes cloudy, then carefully transfer the aqueous upper phase to a new LoBind tube (expected volume ≈2.0 mL).

steps.title: Ethanol precipitation and DNA recovery
steps.instruction: Add 0.1 vol 3 M sodium acetate pH 5.2, invert gently; add ~3 vol 100 % ethanol, invert 10–15 times; precipitate DNA at –80 °C ≥1 h (or –20 °C overnight). Pre‑cool centrifuge to 4 °C, centrifuge 16,000 × g, 4 °C for 30 min, discard supernatant, wash pellet with 4 mL 80 % ethanol (2 mL if using 2 mL tubes), centrifuge 16,000 × g, 4 °C for 5 min, discard supernatant, wash with 2 mL 70 % ethanol, centrifuge 5 min, discard, remove all liquid, spin briefly, air‑dry 3–5 min (do not overdry). Resuspend pellet in 52 µL TE pH 8.0; if multiple pellets, dissolve sequentially and combine. Incubate RT 5 min with occasional inversion, brief spin, pool into a single 1.5 mL LoBind tube, store 4 °C short‑term or –20 °C long‑term, quantify with Qubit DNA HS assay, then proceed to size‑selection.

steps.title: Size selection – standard AMPure
steps.instruction: Add 0.45× volume AMPure PB beads to the 3C DNA sample, mix thoroughly, incubate 10 min at RT, place on a magnetic rack until clear (~5 min), discard supernatant, wash beads twice with 200 µL 80 % ethanol (do not overdry), elute DNA in 47 µL Low TE pH 8.0, incubate 5 min, place on magnet, and transfer eluate to a new tube.

steps.title: Size selection – diluted beads
steps.instruction: Prepare a 35 % (v/v) bead dilution: mix 1.75 mL AMPure PB beads with 3.25 mL Elution Buffer and store at 4 °C (up to 30 days). Add 3.1× volume of the diluted beads to the sample, mix, spin briefly, incubate 10 min at RT, place on magnet, discard supernatant, wash beads twice with 200 µL 80 % ethanol, air‑dry briefly (do not overdry), resuspend in 50 µL elution buffer, incubate 5 min, place on magnet, and transfer supernatant to a new tube.

steps.title: Gel and Femto Pulse QC
steps.instruction: Run undigested, digested, and 3C products on a 1 % agarose gel. Analyze 0.5 ng/µL DNA using a Femto Pulse instrument and confirm the expected fragment‑size distribution.

steps.title: General handling notes
steps.instruction: Always use wide‑bore tips, keep reagents thawed and mixed as directed, avoid overdrying beads, maintain accurate temperature control, ensure crosslinked pellets are free of residual liquid before reactions, and use DNA LoBind tubes to minimize loss. KOD Xtreme polymerase may be replaced with PrimeStar LongSeq DNA polymerase (catalog R055A).

steps.title: Adjust size‑selection thresholds
steps.instruction: Optional: for Revio/Sequel II platforms, perform BluePippin high‑pass selection (≥5 kb) per manufacturer instructions, or use the 35 % diluted AMPure PB method (3.1×) to retain fragments ≈3–5 kb (same procedure as the “Size selection – diluted beads” step).
